title: Tenant observability mosaic: adaptive collectors, Kafka bridging, and KS-map index
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: Private and Dedicated customers are asking for tighter isolation of telemetry while keeping operator overhead low. Current approaches either run per-tenant collectors (high resource) or a shared forwarder with coarse sharding (risking tenant bleed and poor trace continuity). This ticket proposes a new "mosaic" architecture: a light-weight tenant adapter at the ingress, a compact KS-map index (tenant keyspace to pipeline mapping), and an optional Kafka-based bridging layer for on-prem clusters that need durable handoff and cross-datacenter fanout.

Goals:
- Provide tenant-level logical isolation for traces, metrics, and logs without N x resource scaling.
- Preserve full distributed trace continuity (trace IDs, span relationships) across tenant boundaries and collector hops.
- Support air-gapped or intermittently-connected on-prem clusters via durable Kafka bridging with configurable retention.
- Add per-tenant adaptive sampling and dynamic redaction rules to control ingest costs and compliance needs.
- Expose latency/error and ingress health dashboards for operators and per-tenant owners.

Success metrics:
- End-to-end ingest latency increase <= 50ms P50 and <= 150ms P99 for normal load at ingress path in dedicated deployments.
- Memory overhead per host < 350MB for the mosaic adapter under 10k TPS.
- Kafka bridging durable handoff verified for 99.9% of messages during transient network partitions in integration tests.
- Per-tenant sampling reduces tokenized cost by at least 20% for selected heavy tenants during pilot.

Design/approach summary:
1) Mosaic ingress adapter (go): lightweight process co-located with perimeter forwarder. It performs tenant identification, enforces tenant-specific redaction rules, attaches tenant-scoped trace metadata (tenant id hashed into a tenant namespace header), and consults local KS-map index for routing.
2) KS-map index: compact local datastore (LMDB) holding routing rules for tenant -> pipeline (collector instance, kafka topic, or remote forwarder). The index is updated via control-plane push (signed manifest) and supports fast lookups.
3) Kafka bridge (optional): for on-prem air-gapped sites, the adapter writes to a local Kafka cluster (topic per-shard) with schema-enforced envelopes. A bridge consumer in the cloud reads durable topics and materializes telemetry into the central ingest pipeline. Bridge supports at-least-once delivery, idempotency keys, and tombstones for GDPR deletions.
4) Adaptive sampling & sampler-controller: controller in control plane distributes sampling policies; the adapter enforces probabilistic and reservoir sampling. Sampling decisions attach sampling metadata so traces can be re-hydrated for end-to-end analysis.
5) Observability & dashboards: new per-tenant dashboards (ingest-rate, dropped-rate, tail-latency, kafka-lag when enabled), a central error-rate alerting rule, and a diagnostic trace-viewer for mosaic-handled traces.

Implementation plan:
- Spike (Week 1): implement a minimal go adapter that performs tenant tag and LMDB-based KS lookup. Stand up a local Kafka in CI and prototype the envelope format.
- Core (Weeks 2-4): implement KS-map updater, sampling enforcement, and end-to-end pipeline to staging central ingest. Add unit + integration tests and perf harness.
- Harden (Week 5): add redaction rules engine, idempotency for Kafka bridge, and signing for KS manifests. Run chaos tests for network partitions.
- Dashboarding + rollout (Weeks 6-7): build Grafana panels and SLO rules, run a pilot with two customers on Dedicated and one air-gapped on Private. Gradual rollout with canary.

Acceptance_criteria:
acceptance_criteria: Adapter tags tenant and routes to correct pipeline per KS-map in staging
KS-map updates delivered and applied within 30s of control-plane push in normal conditions
Kafka bridge preserves order per-tenant shard and recovers after simulated broker downtime with <1% message loss in CI tests
Dashboards show per-tenant ingest rate, drop rate, P50/P99 ingest latency and kafka-lag when enabled
Pilot customers confirm no observable regression in application-side trace continuity
testing_plan: Unit tests for adapter routing and redaction rules
Integration harness: local Kafka + staging ingest to validate durable handoff
Performance tests: synthetic load at 10k TPS; measure memory/latency overhead
Chaos tests: network partition + delayed KS-manifest delivery
End-to-end trace continuity verification using end-to-end trace replays
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: KS-map staleness could route to wrong pipeline -> Mitigation: fallback default pipeline and alert when manifest TTL exceeded
Risk: Kafka bridge increases operational burden in air-gapped sites -> Mitigation: provide a managed bootstrap script and runbook with health-checks and retention recommendations
Risk: Redaction rules incorrectly remove critical fields -> Mitigation: sandboxed rule testing and per-tenant dry-run mode
rollout_plan: 1) Internal alpha: infra + platform teams on dedicated cluster (1 host per region)
2) Customer pilot: enable for 2 low-to-medium traffic tenants with feature flag; monitor dashboards and error budgets
3) Gradual enablement: expand tenant coverage and enable Kafka bridge for one private customer; maintain canary fallback to shared forwarder
4) Full enablement: GA after 8 weeks of pilot with observed stability
